title: Game Math Part 2 · Rendering 2: Camera View, Zoom and Output Windows

scenes.title: 카메라를 바꾸는 네 가지 질문
lines: Why do moving a camera and changing its zoom give different views of the same world?
First, real split-screen gameplay will help separate cameras from output windows, followed by a pixel-aspect calculation.
Then we connect field of view with zoom numerically and compare that with moving the camera forward.
Finally, orthographic projection and a split-screen exercise will show which parameters to change.

scenes.title: 같은 게임의 두 화면을 따로 보기
lines: Split Fiction divides the two players at a central boundary. Follow each character in its own view.
Different directions produce different backgrounds and occlusion; these are more than identical pieces of one picture.
The camera determines the view; the output window determines where that result goes.
We will calculate with our own defined diagram rather than infer this game’s internal settings.

scenes.title: 그림을 저장할 곳과 놓을 영역
lines: A render target stores rendering results, either in a display buffer or a texture used by another calculation.
Our output rectangle uses a top-left origin with pixel coordinates increasing rightward and downward.
Store the rectangle’s position and width and height separately. Split a1920-by1080 image vertically.
The left window begins at(0,0) with size960 by1080; the right begins at(960,0) with the same size.
The left window’s last integer column is959; position plus width gives the next boundary at960.
One camera result may appear in two windows, or different camera results may occupy them. Storage and viewing are separate choices.
Shadow maps and in-world monitors can store results in textures. Implementation and the full pixel transformation come in the next lecture.

scenes.title: 화면 비율과 픽셀 비율을 나누기
lines: A1920-by1080 image has aspect16:9; an individual pixel is not16:9.
If display and resolution both have aspect16:9, a physical pixel has equal width and height:1:1.
Multiply physical display width-to-height by resolution height-to-width; all aspect ratios here use width divided by height.
A4:3 pixel array stretched across a16:9 physical area gives physical pixel aspect4/3.
A circle drawn assuming square pixels becomes horizontally stretched. Fixing that with camera rotation or object scale breaks other relationships.
Moving or splitting a window does not change physical pixel aspect, although the rectangle’s aspect changes.
Off-screen bitmaps commonly assume square pixels; an anamorphic plan must record the later display stretch.
The source’s1153-by720 is not exactly16:10;1152-by720 is. Verify ratios rather than memorize resolution lists.

scenes.title: 건물의 모양과 화면의 움직임
lines: Townscaper moves from a small waterside building to a closer view. Choose a roof corner and window as landmarks.
Orbiting reveals sides and stairs. A changed appearance does not mean physical pixel aspect changed.
Adding blocks changes the building itself. Distinguish construction from changes of viewpoint.
Tracking the same roof shows parts coming forward or being hidden; camera position and direction change how the scene reads.
These pixels alone do not establish the game’s projection matrix or numeric zoom method.
Our original diagram can hold position, field of view and output rectangle fixed and change one at a time.
Keep the overlap of the building faces in mind as we construct the camera’s potential viewing volume.

scenes.title: 카메라가 보는 공간은 입체입니다
lines: The screen is flat, but a perspective camera’s potential view is a volume. Begin with four corner rays.
Cut the pyramid by near and far planes to obtain the view frustum.
A point inside is only potentially visible: an opaque object may still occlude it.
Moving translates the volume, rotating changes its orientation and changing FOV changes its opening.
Moving the output rectangle rightward is different: the same view may simply be placed elsewhere.
We will classify inside and outside with the six boundary planes, beyond the outline of a pyramid.

scenes.title: 여섯 클립 평면으로 안쪽 고르기
lines: A frustum has left,right,top,bottom,near and far boundaries; each boundary is an infinite plane.
Choose the inner half-space of each plane and retain their intersection.
Our example faces positive z with near1 and far11; these are defined values, not measurements of the game.
Points at z0.5,z6 and z12 are before near,between the distance planes and beyond far.
Being at z6 is insufficient if x extends beyond a side boundary at that depth.
A triangle crossing a boundary may retain a portion. One outside vertex does not justify deleting the whole primitive.
Near and far also affect depth precision; the actual depth format and projection convention matter.
The next lecture calculates depth and division order; retain both distance boundaries and four screen-side boundaries.

scenes.title: 시점이 돌아도 같은 건물을 추적하기
lines: Floors are added while a low view reveals the building’s side. Observe empty screen space and the roof boundary.
An elevated view reveals roofs and terraces; entering the view and becoming unoccluded are different events.
Walls overlapping frontally separate in an oblique view; the same spatial relationship gives a different arrangement.
Later framing becomes wider and closer again. Record apparent size separately from which faces are visible.
Leaving the image does not prove that the building vanished; consider the viewing volume.
The recording does not reveal numeric near or far planes. Keep observed pixels separate from defined math examples.
Our next diagram holds camera position fixed while changing FOV, isolating it from movement.

scenes.title: 시야각은 얼마나 벌어지는 각도일까요?
lines: In a top view, connect the camera to the left and right boundaries; their whole angle is horizontal FOV.
The angle from the center to either edge is half the FOV:45 degrees for a90-degree horizontal view.
At depth3, the half-width is3 times tan45 degrees, or3.
The horizontal span at that depth runs from−3 to3, width6; at depth6 it becomes12.
A smaller FOV captures less at the same depth; the same object occupies a larger fraction of the image.
Horizontal and vertical FOV are distinct; an aspect ratio links them, but equal numeric angles are a separate choice.

scenes.title: 줌 두 배가 되는 시야각 계산
lines: The source defines zoom relative to90-degree FOV as one divided by tan of the half-angle.
For90 degrees, tan45 is1, giving zoom1 as our reference.
Zoom2 requires half-angle tangent0.5; FOV is twice arctan of one half.
The result is about53.13 degrees, not45: FOV and zoom are not linearly proportional.
With camera and objects fixed, central image sizes double because the captured range narrows.
Check whether tangent functions accept radians; passing degree values directly changes the result.
This zoom is a projection parameter; orthographic zoom has a different meaning and units.

scenes.title: 캐릭터 크기와 함께 보이는 공간
lines: The players cross the candy town from different positions. Compare character size with the surrounding paths in view.
A larger character does not prove a different FOV: distance,direction and scene arrangement may also differ.
The gameplay supplies an observation question; controlled examples isolate position and angle.

scenes.title: 두 시야각을 화면 비율로 연결하기
lines: For square pixels in a16:9 window, horizontal zoom1 requires vertical zoom16/9 to preserve shape.
Horizontal FOV is90 degrees; vertical FOV is twice arctan(9/16), about58.72 degrees.
A wider window captures a larger horizontal angle; using90 degrees on both axes can stretch a circle horizontally.
Vertical-to-horizontal zoom equals the window’s physical aspect; nonsquare pixels need more than pixel counts.
Include any physical display stretch in addition to1920-by1080 counts; this connects the pixel-aspect calculation.
If an engine exposes one FOV parameter, check whether it is horizontal or vertical and how aspect derives the other.
Resizing may preserve horizontal or vertical FOV; verify what becomes visible or disappears.

scenes.title: 확대 전후 같은 지붕을 따라가기
lines: Track one roof while the waterside structure grows, separating newly constructed faces.
Wider framing changes to a closer view: the roof grows while less surrounding water fits in the image.
Compare roofs at other depths as well as the foreground target.
We will not label this game’s input as zoom or movement; a defined two-depth example will calculate the distinction.

scenes.title: 앞으로 이동하면 모든 물체가 두 배일까요?
lines: Place equal-sized panels at forward depths4 and8; perspective size is proportional to object size and inversely proportional to depth.
Doubling zoom without moving the camera doubles both panels while preserving their relative image-size ratio.
Move the camera forward2 at fixed zoom: depths change4→2 and8→6.
The near panel grows by4/2=2; the far grows by8/6=4/3, changing their relative image sizes.
Both methods can double the front panel, but the rear differs; camera movement and lens zoom are different.
The denominator is forward-axis z, not the Euclidean distance to an off-axis point.
Use landmarks at multiple depths; one target can hide changes in their relationship.

scenes.title: 렌즈와 센서에서 시야각 구하기
lines: Physical-camera FOV depends on sensor size as well as focal length; consider sensor width.
Horizontal FOV is twice arctan of sensor width divided by twice focal length, using consistent units.
A36mm-wide sensor with18mm focal length gives ratio1 and horizontal FOV90 degrees.
Keeping the sensor and using36mm focal length gives ratio0.5 and FOV about53.13 degrees.
An18mm sensor width at18mm focal length gives the same FOV; one number alone is insufficient.
Distinguish an arbitrary mathematical projection-plane distance from the physical lens focal length.
Check sensor,focal length and fit policy in physical-camera settings. These calculations address FOV, not depth of field or lens distortion.

scenes.title: 가까운 면과 먼 건물을 같이 보기
lines: Use a large wall and rear roof as landmarks, separating newly added geometry from orbit-revealed faces.
Close framing emphasizes the wall; wide framing includes water and other structures.
Changing orientation affects visible area beyond a simple enlargement factor; record viewpoint conditions.
The next interval adds blocks around an upper terrace; distinguish existing railings from new walls.
Wider framing returns to a close view; track front and rear landmarks together.
We do not infer game camera calls; our factors2 and4/3 belong to the defined diagram, not this recording.
Gameplay motivates a readable result; the mathematical example isolates its changed variables. Connect them while respecting the evidence.
If distance-based shrinking is unwanted, maps and modeling drawings can use another projection.

scenes.title: 직교 투영에서는 투영선이 평행합니다
lines: Perspective rays meet at the camera; orthographic projection lines are parallel.
Equal panels at depths2 and10 shrink differently in perspective but have equal orthographic image sizes.
Orthographic projection does not preserve all shape: rotating a panel reduces its projected width and collapses viewing-direction information.
Moving along the viewing direction leaves surviving image sizes unchanged; clipping and occlusion still require checks.
Its viewing volume is a box, described by width and height rather than an opening angle.
A constant scale is useful for maps and drawings. This proof uses our diagram; Townscaper’s actual projection remains unverified.

scenes.title: 직교 상자의 크기로 줌 계산하기
lines: Use an orthographic box8 by4.5 with aspect16:9 and a1920-by1080 output.
Mapping width8 to1920 pixels gives240 pixels per world unit; check the same scale vertically.
Halve both dimensions to4 by2.25 for480 pixels per unit, doubling image size without moving forward.
The source’s orthographic zoom is2 divided by size:0.25 for width8 and0.5 for width4.
Perspective zoom comes from an angle ratio; orthographic zoom corresponds to inverse world length.
Changing only width creates unequal scales and turns a circle into an ellipse; preserve physical output aspect.
Orthographic rendering still uses near,far and depth comparison; absence of shrinking does not remove depth.

scenes.title: 정면과 지붕 위 시점을 나누어 보기
lines: More construction and viewpoint changes reveal terrace walls and roofs. Separate frontal and overhead views.
Reading a different face requires another direction; enlargement alone cannot reveal every hidden roof or wall.
The orthographic diagram demonstrated a constant scale as an option, not an inferred property of the game.
Choose viewing direction,perspective and range before dividing the output; our next problem returns to two player windows.

scenes.title: 두 플레이어 화면에서 유지할 값 정하기
lines: Start with square pixels,1920 by1080,horizontal FOV90,zoomX1 and zoomY16/9.
Each vertical half is960 by1080 with aspect8:9 rather than16:9.
Preserve vertical FOV and zoomY; their zoom ratio must become8/9.
This gives zoomX2 and horizontal FOV about53.13 degrees, narrowing the visible sides.
Preserving horizontal FOV instead is another choice; declare the preserved axis before validating shape and range.
For the orthographic exercise,8 by4.5 gives240 pixels per unit;4 by2.25 doubles it in the same output.
Neither exercise moved the camera forward; name output-aspect and projection changes separately in code.

scenes.title: 건축과 관찰을 따로 기록하기
lines: The final example changes from a close roof and frontal view to wider,elevated framing.
Later blocks change the building itself. New faces differ from existing faces revealed by another view.
Write what to observe,from which direction,over what range and in which output window.
Change one condition and compare the same landmarks to check both readability and the camera calculation.

scenes.title: 시야·줌·출력 창의 계산을 정리하기
lines: We separated what a camera sees from where the result goes: position,direction,projection range and output rectangle are related but distinct.
Square pixels can form a16:9 image; the two zoom axes must match physical window aspect.
Zoom2 changed90 degrees to about53.13; moving forward instead changes objects at different depths by different factors.
Orthographic projection uses box size instead of FOV; occlusion,clipping and axis scales still matter.
Record window size and the preserved FOV axis,compare multiple depths and avoid inferring game internals from pixels.
Next we follow one point from local space through clip space to a screen pixel,using these camera and output choices as inputs.
